# Tensile test elastic modulus analysis

Elastic modulus was estimated as the slope of an ordinary least squares linear fit of stress against strain. The fit for each material pooled all 30 measurements from its three specimens and used the full measured strain interval (0.0002–0.0020); the fitted intercept was not constrained to zero. The reported modulus is the slope converted from MPa to GPa. The plot shows individual measurements and the pooled fit for each material.

| Material | Specimens | Modulus (GPa) | Fit intercept (MPa) | R² | Per-specimen slopes (mean ± SD, GPa) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 3 | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 | 69.38 ± 1.76 |
| Steel | 3 | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 | 199.06 ± 2.00 |
| Titanium | 3 | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 | 116.56 ± 1.71 |

The pooled fits are strongly linear over the measured interval (R² ≈ 0.998). Steel has the highest estimated modulus, followed by titanium and aluminum. Per-specimen slope variation is summarized as the sample standard deviation across the three specimens. These estimates characterize this dataset and fitting interval; they do not account for uncertainty in specimen geometry or instrument calibration.

![Stress–strain measurements and pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.png)
